purpose: isolate which maintained unlabeled/domain-adaptation loss components are responsible for the slight regression of the stable v2 CD pipeline relative to source-initialized supervised finetuning
evidence_supported_conclusions: No isolated maintained loss component improves the 5-seed mean over simple source-initialized supervised finetuning on FD001_TO_FD004.
Among the tested single components, monotonic-only and pseudo-only are the least harmful on the mean, while MMD-only and source-stage-only are slightly more harmful.
Adding source-stage supervision back on top of pseudo does not recover the gap, so pseudo-only underperformance is not explained mainly by the absence of a supervised stage head.

The seed ordering is highly stable across all variants: seed 44 remains the easiest and seed 43 remains the hardest, which indicates the current loss family mostly shifts the same partition difficulty landscape instead of changing it.
Relative to source-init-only, the full current CD pipeline helps only seed 44 and hurts seeds 42, 43, 45, and 46 in this matched FD001_TO_FD004 comparison.

A narrower supported interpretation is that the current FD001_TO_FD004 regression is not caused by one catastrophic auxiliary term alone; it is a distributed small-regression pattern across the present loss family, with task/partition sensitivity still dominating.
important_caveat: These controls are matched to the stable bare/pre v2 FD001_TO_FD004 line; they isolate maintained loss components within that branch rather than proving the same ranking for all architectures.
